recipes.name: Apple, Cranberry, and Pear Crisp
ingredients_raw: 2 Rome Beauty apples - peeled, cored, and cubed
2 medium Comice pears - peeled, cored, and cubed
0.5 cup unsalted butter, cut into pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease an 8-inch baking dish.
Mix apples, pears, cranberries, honey, lemon juice, and 1 tablespoon flour together in the prepared dish.
Mix 1/2 cup flour, brown sugar, oats, and walnuts together in a medium bowl. Cut in butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Sprinkle over fruit mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown and crisp on top, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple, Cranberry, and Pear Crisp
raw_recipe.description: This apple, cranberry, and pear crisp is a splendid concoction of fresh and dried fruit topped with a decadent buttered walnut topping.

review.reviewBody: Complete silence descended on the table as folks dug in to this dessert! It was so delicious for fall. I changed a couple things--added 2 extra pears, so therefore increased the rest of the ingredients (except apples) by 50%. I didn't have walnuts, so used pecans. One tip is to mix the topping ingredients in the food processor--just pulse until it looks like coarse crumbs--fast and easy.

Fantastic. Here's how I modified it:

-Used sweet-tart apples (one of the NY# varieties) and cranberries, no pears.
-Grated about 2 tbsp of fresh ginger. Added to fruit with some cinnamon.
-Subbed maple syrup for the honey.
-Took out some of the sugar in the topping and used pitted dates instead. Pulsed in the food processor with some powdered ginger and more cinnamon, and a pinch of salt.

Came out awesome, although the date chunks were a little too hard/chewy.
Outstanding! I didn't have pears and used fresh cranberries instead of dried. TIP: for the topping, I grated the cold butter on a cheese grater. An easy and quick way to get an even consistency. Yum!

I made this tonight because I had a bunch of aged pears to use up. I loved it -- with some changes. I used all pears (sliced, not cubed) and used fresh cranberries instead of dried. I pulsed the cranberries in the food processor a couple times and tossed them with the pears, and added some cinnamon and nutmeg. I omitted the lemon juice. As for the topping, I halved the butter, flour, brown sugar and oats. Also omitted the nuts (out of sheer laziness)and put a bit of cinnamon in for good measure. The result was fantastic - not too sweet - and the cranberry flavor really put it over the top. Thanks for the idea!

It got rave reviews and it was gobbled up over yummy noises. I took the recommendation to make the topping in the food processor which came out as a thick goo. It worked out ok - but it didn't have the crisp topping - too much butter. I would recommend reducing that a bit - someone mentioned they used 5T that may be a good plan. I did add the cinnamon and nutmeg, (1 tsp each) which added some depth to the flavor. A little vanilla ice cream (or cinnamon if you have it) and it is well received.

Wow! So very yummy! After reading the reviews I decided to incorporate into the recipe what I thought were great suggestions. I did use my food processor to do the "mix" portion of the recipe. I did cube the fruit and used 3 pears as they needed to be "moved along". I had fresh nutmeg and grated it into the dry topping ingredients...probably a tsp. I did measure the brown sugar but "skimped" on the measurement some...thought we really don't need all that sugar. And finally I served it with vanilla ice cream while still warm. OMG....Sooooo good. I was suprised how much it made...probably due to the fact that I added that extra pear.

Yummmm. What a quick and delicious dish. I used Bartlett pears and Granny Smith apples. To decrease the calories a bit I used 1 T. honey, 1/3 cup brown sugar and 5 T. butter without any significant compromise to the wonderful taste. When I got to step 3 and to make it a little faster, I placed the walnuts in the processor and pulsed to a chunky ground. Then, I added the flour, sugar, oats and butter and briefly processed it to a crumb consistency, before sprinkling it over the fruit. I made this dish in a glass pie plate and it was crisp and brown in 30 minutes. I served with vanilla bean ice cream. Wonderful. Later, I zapped a helping in the microwave for 45 seconds to reheat it. Well, the rest is history. This will definitely go into my 10 star file. Thanks for sharing, Barb.

Had five overripe Bartlett pears and one sorry looking Gala apple leftover from a lunch box, plus one Gerber baby applesauce and a cup of frozen cranberries (bought fresh yesterday, so not craisins). Tossed all of them together with a bit of cinnamon in addition to the honey (a little bit less due to the applesauce) and flour. Then made the crisp topping with a bit of cinnamon. Oh my stars. I am not even a big fan of pears, but this was phenomenal. Deserves far more than five stars. Eternal thanks for a fab recipe!

Oh so warm and delicious - this got a 5 star rating in my house. I made mild enhancements....added a little more pear, cinnamon and then mixed everything in step 2 before pouring into the dish. Then I made 1.5x of the crust. We have a nut allergy so omitted the nuts and it was soooo yummy. Will be a go to for sure in the fall w/ a scoop of caramel ice cream. Note - We live at altitude so added 10 degrees to the cooking temp and cooked a bit longer to ensure the crunchy crisp. Thank you!

This is so delicious, if you look at my photo, that is what was left on a dessert table of at least 20 desserts!
I used a walnut crust under the fruit in addition to the chopped walnuts in the topping. I added cinnamon to the topping and the fruit. Try just using the pears and omitting the apples, and serve alamode w vanilla ice cream.

This was a great twist! We had some fresh golden delicious apples from our local orchard, so I used 4 of those instead of 2. Two Bartlett pears, and a little over 1/4 cup of sweetened dried cranberries. I can't do butter, so I added a teaspoon of imitation butter flavoring and 3 spoonfuls of melted Crisco to make the topping instead. Sprinkled cinnamon generously over the top & baked in an 11"x7" glass dish for just under 40 minutes. Very nice taste! Served it with frozen cool whip lite (can't do ice cream either) - it was a hit! Thx for the great recipe - I'd have never thought to use honey in this way!

Great recipe. I had a lot of pears so used enough pears sliced to almost fill a 9 by 9 dish, added one sliced apple and a cup of raspberries. Love it. The pears and raspberries were a perfect combination.

Great and super easy! I added about a tablespoon of corn starch to the fruit mix and a tablespoon or so of orange juice to the fruit. Also substituted cashews for the walnuts and it was perfect! So yummy!

I have made this recipe every year, at least once, for more than a decade. Other than adding cinnamon and apple pie spice, I make it pretty much as written. It's far better than an apple pie or just an apple crisp. So much flavor!
The apples, pears and cranberries are a great combination. The walnuts in the crumble is a great idea.

I made this with Bartlett pears and cranberries only, since that's what was on hand. Everybody loved it. this may be my go-to crumble recipe for everything with this type of toping. it was incredibly easy to make and came out perfect!
It was easy to make and has good flavor. As others suggested, I added some cinnamon and nutmeg to the topping.
I made this over Christmas it was a big hit
